claims.text: The starting Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti alloy is equiatomic.
The starting material is an as-cast, quenched polycrystalline bulk alloy.
The Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti alloy system has a body-centered-cubic structure.
The Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti alloy has substantial intrinsic chemical or structural disorder, with its elements randomly distributed on the lattice.
Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti-family high-entropy alloys can become superconducting below 10 K.
Superconductivity in this alloy family occurs in the dirty limit, where the coherence length exceeds the electron scattering length.
The superconducting phase is approximately a weak-coupling, phonon-mediated BCS superconductor.
Thermal annealing systematically changes local chemical ordering, grain-boundary structure, and the formation or dissolution of short-range clusters in this alloy.
Changes in local chemical disorder, grain boundaries, and clusters alter both the electron mean free path and the phonon spectrum.
Moderate annealing produces lattice softening that enhances electron-phonon coupling.
The annealing-induced enhancement of electron-phonon coupling increases the superconducting transition temperature.
Excessive disorder or excessive annealing increases impurity scattering and pair breaking, thereby suppressing superconductivity.
Insufficient annealing leaves the electron-phonon interaction suboptimal and produces a lower transition temperature than optimal intermediate annealing.
An intermediate annealing treatment, suggested to be near 900 degrees Celsius for an optimal duration, will raise Tc relative to the as-cast state.
Tc will depend nonmonotonically on annealing, with lower values for little and excessive annealing and a peak at intermediate annealing.
Optimally annealed samples will show clearer superconducting-gap signatures and reproducible shifts in Hc1 and Hc2 relative to the as-cast state.

The proposed mechanism should apply to bulk polycrystalline BCC samples in the dirty limit below 10 K at ambient pressure, provided annealing causes no secondary phases or major structural transformations.
Prior measurements on Ta-Nb-Zr-Hf-Ti-family films found that observed Tc variations could not be explained by disorder effects.
